instruction: Can you open our status page and tell me the current uptime for the API?
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the status page.
2. Read the API component's uptime figure.
3. Report the number back.

**Step 1 — Thought:** The status page lives at status.acme.io, so I can load it directly.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://status.acme.io")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** HTTP 200; title `Acme Status`. Banner reads `All Systems Operational`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** The API row carries the figure I need.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="#component-api .uptime")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Text is `99.98% uptime (30 days)`.

**Final answer:** Acme reports the API at 99.98% uptime over the last 30 days, with all systems operational.

instruction: Go to the docs and jump straight to the pagination section using the in-page anchor.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the guide page.
2. Jump to the #pagination anchor.
3. Confirm the right section is showing.

**Step 1 — Thought:** The guide is at docs.example.com/guide and anchors resolve without a click.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://docs.example.com/guide#pagination")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Page loaded; viewport scrolled so the `Pagination` heading sits at y=120.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Verify I actually landed in the right section.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="h2#pagination")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Heading text is `Pagination`.

**Final answer:** Opened https://docs.example.com/guide#pagination and confirmed the viewport sits on the `Pagination` section.

instruction: Compare the pricing of our three main competitors and tell me who is cheapest for 10 seats.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Open the three pricing pages in separate tabs.
2. Extract the 10-seat price from each.
3. Pick the cheapest.

**Step 1 — Thought:** I'll open the first competitor in the active tab.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://rival-a.example/pricing")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Loaded `Pricing - Rival A`; per-seat tile visible.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Open the second in a new tab so the first stays put.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://rival-b.example/pricing", new_tab=True)`
**Step 2 — Observation:** New tab opened; title `Rival B | Plans`.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Same for the third.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://rival-c.example/pricing", new_tab=True)`
**Step 3 — Observation:** New tab opened; title `Rival C Pricing`.

**Step 4 — Thought:** Read each plan tile's per-seat cost.
**Step 4 — Action:** `browser_extract(selector=".plan .price", attributes=["data-seats", "data-amount"])`
**Step 4 — Observation:** At 10 seats: Rival A $12, Rival B $9, Rival C $11.

**Final answer:** For 10 seats Rival B is cheapest at $9/seat, ahead of Rival C ($11) and Rival A ($12).

instruction: I closed the tab with the article I was reading. Can you find it again in history?
output:
**Plan:**
1. Open the browser history.
2. Locate the recently closed article.
3. Reopen it and confirm the title.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Open the history page to see recent entries.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="chrome://history")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** History lists the 20 most recent visits.

**Step 2 — Thought:** The article was about rate limiting; filter the list.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector=".history-entry:has-text('rate limiting')")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** One match: `Designing Resilient Rate Limiters` at devblog.example.com, visited 4 minutes ago.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Reopen that URL.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://devblog.example.com/posts/resilient-rate-limiters")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** Page loaded; title `Designing Resilient Rate Limiters`.

**Final answer:** Recovered the closed article `Designing Resilient Rate Limiters` at devblog.example.com/posts/resilient-rate-limiters.

instruction: Follow the redirect on our old wiki link /old-onboarding and tell me where it ends up.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Request the old path.
2. Observe the redirect chain.
3. Report the final URL.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Hit the old path directly and watch the hops.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://wiki.acme.io/old-onboarding")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** 302 to /handbook/onboarding, then 301 to /handbook/onboarding-2026, then 200.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Confirm the URL the address bar settles on.
**Step 2 — Action:** `page_screenshot(path="/tmp/agent/redirect_final.png")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Address bar shows https://wiki.acme.io/handbook/onboarding-2026.

**Final answer:** `/old-onboarding` redirects through two hops and finally resolves to https://wiki.acme.io/handbook/onboarding-2026.

instruction: Open the shop, go back two pages, then forward one, and tell me where I land.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Build up a small history stack.
2. Go back twice.
3. Go forward once.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Start at the shop home.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://shop.example.com/")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Loaded `Shop - Home`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Visit a category to add a history entry.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="a[href='/category/laptops']")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Navigated to `Laptops`.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Open a product as well.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="a.product-link:nth-of-type(1)")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** Navigated to `ThinkPad X1`.

**Step 4 — Thought:** Now step back twice.
**Step 4 — Action:** `browser_back()`
**Step 4 — Observation:** First back -> `Laptops`; second back -> `Shop - Home`.

**Step 5 — Thought:** Then go forward once.
**Step 5 — Action:** `browser_back(forward=True)`
**Step 5 — Observation:** Forward -> `Laptops`.

**Final answer:** After two backs and one forward I land on the `Laptops` category page.

instruction: Open the dashboard SPA, switch to the Reports route, then reload and check the route survives.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the SPA shell.
2. Switch routes client-side.
3. Reload and confirm the deep link persists.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Load the SPA.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://app.acme.io/dashboard")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Shell rendered; URL /dashboard, title `Acme Console`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Click the Reports nav item, which routes client-side.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="nav a[data-route='reports']")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** URL changed to /reports without a full reload; heading `Reports`.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Reload to test deep-link persistence.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_press(key="F5")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** After reload the URL is still /reports and the table re-renders.

**Final answer:** The SPA keeps /reports across a reload, so the route is deep-linkable.

instruction: Open the lead news story and click through to the next article; give me its headline.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Open the current lead article.
2. Follow the next-article control.
3. Read the new headline.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Load the lead story.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://news.example.com/2026/10/quantum-battery")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Title `Quantum Battery Breakthrough`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Use the next-article control at the bottom.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="a.next-article")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Navigated to a new article.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Read its headline.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="article h1")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** Headline: `Grid-Scale Storage Gets Cheaper`.

**Final answer:** The next article is `Grid-Scale Storage Gets Cheaper`.

instruction: Go to our GitHub repo and then open the Releases page.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the repo home.
2. Open the Releases tab.
3. Read the latest tag.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Load the repo.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://github.com/acme/web")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Repo page loaded; default branch `main`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Open the Releases tab.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="a[href$='/releases']")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** URL is https://github.com/acme/web/releases.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Read the top release tag.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="section:nth-of-type(1) h2 a")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** Latest release is `v2.4.1`.

**Final answer:** The releases page shows the latest tag v2.4.1.

instruction: On the login page, open the Terms link in a new tab and tell me its effective date.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the sign-in page.
2. Open the footer Terms link (opens in a new tab).
3. Read the effective date.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Load the sign-in page.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://app.acme.io/login")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Email and Password fields visible.

**Step 2 — Thought:** The footer Terms link has target=_blank.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="footer a[href='/legal/terms']")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** New tab opened at /legal/terms.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Read the effective date.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector=".terms-effective-date")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** `Effective date: 1 September 2026`.

**Final answer:** The Terms page effective date is 1 September 2026.

instruction: I have a shortlink at ac.me/launch - where does it actually go?
output:
**Plan:**
1. Request the shortlink.
2. Observe the redirect chain.
3. Report the final URL.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Resolve the shortlink and watch the hops.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://ac.me/launch")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** 302 to https://events.acme.io/webinar/2026-q4, then 200.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Confirm the settled URL.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="link[rel='canonical']", attribute="href")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** canonical = https://events.acme.io/webinar/2026-q4.

**Final answer:** ac.me/launch resolves to https://events.acme.io/webinar/2026-q4.

instruction: Open the product listing and jump to page 4 via the URL.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Navigate with the page query param.
2. Confirm the pagination widget marks page 4 active.
3. Report.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Use the query param to jump straight to page 4.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://shop.example.com/products?page=4")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Grid loaded; 24 items.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Check which page the widget highlights.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector=".pagination .active")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Active page text is `4`.

**Final answer:** Page 4 of the product listing is open with 24 items.

instruction: Fetch the sitemap and tell me how many URLs it lists.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Open the sitemap XML.
2. Count the loc entries.
3. Report the total.

**Step 1 — Thought:** The sitemap is XML at /sitemap.xml.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://blog.example.com/sitemap.xml")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** XML renderer shows a urlset root.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Count the loc entries.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_extract(selector="url > loc", count_only=True)`
**Step 2 — Observation:** 847 <loc> entries.

**Final answer:** The sitemap lists 847 URLs.

instruction: The site defaulted to English; switch me to the German homepage.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Request the German locale directly.
2. Confirm the page language.
3. Report.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Request the German locale directly.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://www.example.com/de/")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Page loaded with `<html lang="de">`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Confirm the content is German.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="h1")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Heading: `Willkommen bei Example`.

**Final answer:** Loaded the German homepage at https://www.example.com/de/.

instruction: Open the saved Runbook bookmark from my bookmarks bar.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Open the bookmarks manager.
2. Click the Runbook entry.
3. Confirm the page.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Open the bookmarks manager.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="chrome://bookmarks")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Bookmarks page lists an `Ops` folder.

**Step 2 — Thought:** The Runbook entry lives in that folder.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="a[title='Incident Runbook']")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Opened https://runbooks.acme.io/incident.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Confirm the destination.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="h1")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** Heading: `Incident Response Runbook`.

**Final answer:** Opened the Runbook bookmark at https://runbooks.acme.io/incident.

instruction: Open Settings via the account dropdown, then use Back to return to the inbox.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the inbox.
2. Open the dropdown and click Settings.
3. Go back to the inbox.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Load the app inbox.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://app.acme.io/inbox")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Inbox loaded; 12 threads.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Reveal the account dropdown.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_hover(selector="#account-menu")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Dropdown expanded; `Settings` item visible.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Click Settings.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="#account-menu a[href='/settings']")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** URL /settings; heading `Settings`.

**Step 4 — Thought:** Return to the inbox.
**Step 4 — Action:** `browser_back()`
**Step 4 — Observation:** Back on /inbox.

**Final answer:** Navigated to Settings, then used Back to return to the inbox.

instruction: That campaign page does a client-side redirect after a couple of seconds - follow it and give me the final URL.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the entry page.
2. Wait for the delayed redirect.
3. Confirm the final URL.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Load the entry page.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://campaign.example.com/welcome")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Loaded `/welcome`; a JS timer is pending.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Wait for the delayed redirect to fire.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_wait_for(seconds=3)`
**Step 2 — Observation:** URL changed to /home.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Confirm the settled URL.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector="link[rel='canonical']", attribute="href")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** canonical = https://campaign.example.com/home.

**Final answer:** The delayed client-side redirect lands on https://campaign.example.com/home.

instruction: Open our marketing homepage and the docs homepage in parallel tabs and tell me which has the longer title.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Open the marketing homepage.
2. Open the docs in a new tab.
3. Compare the two page titles.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Open the marketing homepage.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://www.example.com/")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Title `Example | Build faster`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Open the docs in a new tab.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://docs.example.com/", new_tab=True)`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Title `Example Developer Documentation`.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Compare the title lengths across tabs.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_extract(selector="title", across_tabs=True)`
**Step 3 — Observation:** `Example | Build faster` (22 chars) vs `Example Developer Documentation` (33 chars).

**Final answer:** The docs homepage has the longer title at 33 characters, versus 22 for the marketing homepage.

instruction: Search the docs, open a result, then go back to the results list.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Run a docs search.
2. Open the first result.
3. Return to the results.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Run the search.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://docs.example.com/search?q=webhooks")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** 9 results for `webhooks`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Open the first result.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector=".search-result:nth-of-type(1) a")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Article `Webhooks Overview` loaded.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Return to the results list.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_back()`
**Step 3 — Observation:** Back on the search page; query box still reads `webhooks`.

**Final answer:** Opened the `Webhooks Overview` result, then returned to the search results list.

instruction: Starting at the store homepage, follow the breadcrumb trail down to a sub-category and tell me the full path.
output:
**Plan:**
1. Load the storefront.
2. Click into a top category.
3. Click into a sub-category and read the breadcrumb.

**Step 1 — Thought:** Load the storefront.
**Step 1 — Action:** `browser_navigate(url="https://shop.example.com/")`
**Step 1 — Observation:** Home loaded; top category `Electronics`.

**Step 2 — Thought:** Click into Electronics.
**Step 2 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="nav a[href='/category/electronics']")`
**Step 2 — Observation:** Breadcrumb now `Home / Electronics`.

**Step 3 — Thought:** Then into the Audio sub-category.
**Step 3 — Action:** `browser_click(selector="a[href='/category/electronics/audio']")`
**Step 3 — Observation:** Breadcrumb reads `Home / Electronics / Audio`.

**Step 4 — Thought:** Read the breadcrumb back.
**Step 4 — Action:** `browser_get_text(selector=".breadcrumb")`
**Step 4 — Observation:** `Home / Electronics / Audio`.

**Final answer:** The full breadcrumb path is Home / Electronics / Audio.
